title: An Achievable Rate Region for the Broadcast Channel with Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a communication-theoretic problem, not an education intervention: it studies how feedback can enlarge the achievable rate region of a two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel. The authors ask whether a transmitter can send private and common messages more efficiently when it receives generalized feedback from the receivers, including noiseless, partial, or noisy feedback.

The proposed approach combines Marton coding, block-Markov superposition coding, and joint source-channel coding. In the first phase, fresh information is sent using a Marton-style broadcast strategy; when receivers cannot fully decode, they retain lists of candidate codewords. In the next block, the transmitter sends correlated resolution information to help each receiver disambiguate its list. The key technical contribution is a single-letter achievable rate region for broadcast channels with generalized feedback, with an additional simplified region used for the AWGN case.

The paper analyzes general discrete memoryless broadcast channels and then applies the results to a stochastically degraded AWGN broadcast channel with noisy feedback from only one receiver. It shows that feedback can strictly improve achievable rates relative to the no-feedback capacity region, even when the feedback is noisy. The paper also compares its region with prior results by Bhaskaran, Ozarow-Leung, and Shayevitz-Wigger, and demonstrates that some known examples are recoverable through the new region.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a theoretical information theory/coding paper on broadcast channels with feedback, not an empirical study of educational technology or instructional coaching. It contains no study design, participants, or educational outcomes relevant to the requested topic.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention, teacher outcome, or learner outcome is evaluated, so there is no evidence of impact on education practice or performance.
